holidays.name: Have a Bad Day Day
holidays.description: Today you get a free pass to grumble, groan, and embrace the gloom. It's the cheeky opposite of all those "have a nice day" greetings. Wear mismatched socks, stub your toe dramatically, and sigh at the weather with pride.
holidays.origin: The day was created by Thomas and Ruth Roy of Wellcat Holidays as a playful counterbalance to relentless cheerfulness. It reminds us that bad days are a normal part of being human.
holidays.funFact: Wellcat Holidays, the group behind it, is known for registering many offbeat celebrations. Meanwhile, plenty of people find that officially allowing a bad day makes it feel a lot less bad.

holidays.name: Play Monopoly Day
holidays.description: A day to gather around the board, buy up Boardwalk, and test your family's friendships over rent payments. Dust off the top hat and the thimble, because it's time to negotiate, bluff, and go directly to jail.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the classic real-estate board game that has been played at kitchen tables for generations.
holidays.funFact: Monopoly descends from The Landlord's Game, patented in 1904 by Elizabeth Magie. She designed it to show how land monopolies harm people.

holidays.name: National Blow Bagpipes Day
holidays.description: A day for filling your lungs and your neighborhood with the unmistakable drone of the Great Highland bagpipe. Whether you play or just listen, it's a loud and proud salute to one of music's most dramatic instruments.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors the bagpipe and the pipers who keep the tradition alive.
holidays.funFact: A bagpipe's sound comes from reeds fed by air stored in a bag, so a piper can play continuously without pausing to breathe.
